pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines

prior_suggestions.start_name: Badr El Din (BED) fields, Western Desert (Matrouh Governorate)
prior_suggestions.end_name: BED/Abu Sennan connector (junction feeding the BED/AS-Ameryia trunk), Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: Per the Egypt Oil & Gas Western Desert table the line runs from the Badr El Din (BED) producing fields to the 'BED/Abu Sennan connector', a gathering junction in the Abu Gharadig basin of the northern Western Desert where BED field gas ties into the BED/AS-Ameryia trunk (GEM P3936) toward Ameryia/Alexandria. Both endpoints are corroborated as real: the BED fields sit in Matrouh Governorate (BAPETCO acreage; Zawya/BAPETCO Badr-15 discovery), and the Abu Sennan concession is a 644 km2 block in the Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert (NS Energy). The corridor therefore lies within the northern Western Desert / Abu Gharadig basin, roughly bounded 29.8-30.7 N, 27.5-28.7 E, trending generally eastward from the BED fields to the Abu Sennan connector. I could NOT source precise field/junction coordinates, so point lat/lon are left null rather than fabricated; the ~130 km stated length is itself single-sourced and disputed by GulfPub (which places comparable BED lines at 19-63 km), so even the corridor length is low-confidence. Bound is loose (basin-level).

prior_suggestions.start_name: Badr El Din / El Salam field cluster (Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert)
prior_suggestions.end_name: Abu Sennan field, Western Desert, Egypt
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: Existence is in doubt (see validity), so a route is premature. IF any line exists along this corridor, the OGJ CO2-EOR concept describes CO2-rich gas gathered from four Western Desert plants (Obaiyed, El Salam, Tarek, El Qasr) to a central point in the El Salam area, then a 130-mile line to the Abu Sennan field. All named places sit in the Abu Gharadig basin of the northern Western Desert, administratively spanning Matruh governorate, roughly between ~29.5-30.2 N and ~27.5-28.5 E. I do not have a defensible point geocode for the individual fields, so lat/lon are left null rather than fabricated; the bound is loose (basin-scale, ~1 degree box). Corridor runs generally west/northwest (El Salam/Obaiyed area) to east (Abu Sennan) across the Abu Gharadig oil/gas province.

prior_suggestions.start_name: Karawan gas field (offshore, Temsah Concession, East Nile Delta / Mediterranean Sea)
prior_suggestions.end_name: Existing 32-inch Denise/Temsah export sealine tie-in feeding the El Gamil gas plant near Port Said, Egypt
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: Per egyptoil-gas.com's DEKA feature (verified) and the BP/Eni project descriptions, the Karawan field sits roughly 60 km off the Egyptian coast in the Temsah Concession, East Nile Delta, at about 68 m water depth, and is developed jointly with the nearby Denise field under the Petrobel-operated DEKA project. New subsea sealines from the Karawan/Denise wells tie into the existing 32-inch offshore export network that runs to the El Gamil gas processing plant near Port Said. I could not source a precise field wellhead coordinate, so start_lat/start_lon are left null rather than guessed; Port Said is given only as a defensible, named shore anchor for the tie-in end, not the field itself. This is a loose corridor bound (offshore box roughly north/NNE of Port Said out to ~60-70 km), not a route line — a human routes-repo pass would need an SPE/OnePetro field-development paper or a GEBCO/concession map to tighten it.

hint: GulfPub has only an 18.9 km 'Qarun West - WDGP-S' fragment vs sheet 206 km — the GEM row is probably the longer Qarun evacuation line; research what 206 km refers to.

prior_suggestions.start_name: Faramid (Framid) gas field, East Obayed concession, Western Desert, Egypt
prior_suggestions.end_name: Badr El Din (BAPETCO) gas processing facility, Western Desert, Egypt
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: Short (~38 km) intra-field trunk in the northern Egyptian Western Desert. The Faramid/Faramid South field sits in the East Obayed concession, described by the operator as ~30 km northwest of the Meleiha concession. The line runs from that field to the Badr El Din (BAPETCO) processing company/plant, which handles the produced gas (~24-25 MMcf/d). Bound is only concession-scale: both endpoints are defensibly within the Matruh-governorate Western Desert oil/gas belt (the Obayed-Meleiha-Badr El Din cluster southwest of Alexandria/Marsa Matruh), but no published coordinates or route trace was found, so exact endpoint lat/lon are left null rather than invented.

hint: NORPETCO = North Petroleum Company; Abu Gharadig basin, Western Desert. GulfPub matched only an Abu Qir coastal line (rejected as wrong geography).
